still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through disease codes (diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep apnoea and dementia-risk), never for weight alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, the eleven 2034 under-12 bans are unchanged with no state added, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic, all in points of adults. Ever-used minus current: 47.5 − 35.9 = 11.6 points who used and are off now. Ever-used rose 10.0 points, which are new first-timers; 7.0 are on now and 3.0 have already stopped, in line with one-third one-year persistence on full dose and ~55% on low-dose plans. Current users from the 2034 ever-used pool: 35.9 − 7.0 = 28.9, which leaves 37.5 − 28.9 = 8.6 of that pool off, and 8.6 + 3.0 = 11.6 checks. Of the 28.0 on drug in 2034, ~15.0 stayed on continuously and ~13.0 stopped at least once. About 40% of those 13.0 stops were planned drug holidays, which restart at ~90%; the rest restarted at the parent's 36–47% a year. The off pool was 9.5 + 13.0 = 22.5, and 13.9 of them restarted (22.5 − 8.6). Cycled ever-users: ~6.75 continuing users who already had a prior course (45% of 15.0), plus 13.9 restarters, plus ~0.5 new users who have already cycled, plus ~4.5 of those now off who had cycled before. That makes ≈25.65 / 47.5 ≈ 54%. ~59% of current users are on a second or later course. Age check: 0.20×23 + 0.33×36.5 + 0.24×47 + 0.23×35 = 4.6 + 12.05 + 11.28 + 8.05 ≈ 36.0. Income thirds average 35.8, and the bottom and top thirds bracket the national figure. 35.9% of ~276M adults ≈ 99.1M users, up ~22M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~12.5M (13%, down from 14.5M as employers retreat; mostly diabetes and cardiac codes); Medicare ~18.0M (18%), of which the dementia-risk route is ~6.0M after the Jun 2036 label broadening; Medicaid ~3.8M (4%); legitimate cash ~40.3M (41%); imported, compounded-offshore or counterfeit ~24.5M (25%, up from 15.4M). Sum: 99.1M. Legitimate cash breaks down as ~17.5M weight (swollen by people who lost employer coverage), ~11.0M metabolic/longevity, ~5.0M calm/focus, ~2.3M Reset, ~1.8M alcohol, and ~2.7M cash dementia-prevention among 50–64s and other non-qualifiers, total 40.3M. ~22M current users have a BMI under 30, and ~7M are under 25. Adult obesity is ~30.5%. ~17% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and older adults outside Medicare codes. Off-drug: 11.6 points (~32M adults) are former users. ~38% of current users took at least one planned holiday in 2035–36. Pediatric: ~1.1% of under-18s (12–17s ~2.5%). The under-12 rate is flat in the eleven ban states and drifting down elsewhere on the growth data. ~56% of children live in a household with a current user, and ~7.5M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~18.0M users through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, all under prior authorisation. In Jun 2036 the FDA broadened tirzepatide's dementia-risk label to adults 60+ with obesity, or with BMI 27+ and a cardiometabolic comorbidity, without requiring established CVD. Part D plans cover it because the indication is dementia risk, not weight. FICTIONAL arithmetic at the Dec 2036 run rate: 18.0M × ~$215 average net/month × 12 ≈ $46.4B a year in gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from $36.5B. Of that, the dementia route is ~6.0M × ~$225 × 12 ≈ $16.2B, up from $6.5B. CMS classes bimagrumab as an excluded weight-loss adjunct, so Part D does not pay for it even for 65+ users with documented lean-mass loss. Medicaid: still 7 states for weight use; ~3.8M users, mostly on diabetes codes, with dual-eligibles reaching the dementia label through Part D. Two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide runs $3–25 a month. Since India's B2C export registration took effect in Jan 2035, more parcels move through Dubai and Kathmandu consolidators. Chinese 'reta' vials sell for $25–60, 'cagri' vials for $30–80, and since 2035 'bima' activin-antibody vials sell for $120–220 through biologics research fronts. Canadian and Brazilian generic semaglutide is stable at CAD 40–75 and BRL 150–260. India and China supply ~72% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Employers retreated: weight-management coverage fell 29% → 25% (Nov 2035) → 23% (Nov 2036, Business Group on Health). Firms cited a ~+5–6% pharmacy trend and litigation risk after the Ohio suit survived dismissal. Monitored metabolic tracks fell from 13% to 9% of employers and from 7.4M to ~5.3M enrollees, all inside the 12.5M commercial users. Employer-track MariTide users fell 5.6M → 4.2M, and total MariTide users fell 7.1M → 6.6M as cash partly absorbed the loss. Lifestyle-spending reimbursement of calm and Reset fees fell from 19% to 13% of large employers. Managed decline continued: TrumpRx maintenance is now $169 for the Wegovy pill, $149–189 for Foundayo and $219–259 for injectable Wegovy/Zepbound, while starting orals hold at $149. MariTide cash is $199 and retatrutide $279 at all doses. Bimagrumab list is still $1,150. Lilly's 'Strong' clinic bundle (Zepbound plus monthly bimagrumab infusion, launched Apr 2035) costs $599 a month cash plus $90–180 clinic infusion fees. ~1.4M people are on bimagrumab: ~0.9M bundle cash, ~0.3M commercial PA and ~0.2M on gray 'bima'. The access tiers have hardened: disease codes get coverage, everyone else pays $150–300 cash or $5–60 by mail. Gray regrowth to ~24.5M runs through three channels. Offshore-licensed telehealth prescribers (Mexico, Dominican Republic) ship 'personalised' compounded tirzepatide and retatrutide from 503A and foreign pharmacies. Telegram and WhatsApp networks rerouted around India's parcel registration. Longevity peptide storefronts now sell 'stack' kits pairing reta vials with bima.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, IV muscle-preserving adjunct (bimagrumab), sold since Apr 2035 in Lilly's 'Strong' clinic bundle with tirzepatide; not an incretin
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, with growth-monitoring language; barred for weight indication by statute in eleven states)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults 60+ with obesity, or BMI 27+ with a cardiometabolic comorbidity (tirzepatide; broadened Jun 2036 from the obesity-plus-CVD label)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity microdosing by adults without obesity (~11M licensed cash plus a large gray share)
cash 'brain' prescribing for dementia prevention among 50–64s and lean older adults outside the label (~2.7M licensed, more gray)
calm and focus microdosing (~5M), now marketed around 'holiday-friendly' schedules
compulsion 'Reset' plans for betting, shopping, porn and screens (~2.3M)
gray-market 'reta + bima' stacks in gym and longevity communities
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The cognition driver came through an existing product with a broader label. Lilly's tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out in Mar 2035 at an all-cause dementia HR of ~0.81 over ~3.5 years, with a smaller effect in participants without CVD (HR ~0.86, CI touching 0.98). Lilly filed the broadened sNDA in May 2035, and the FDA approved it in Jun 2036, 13 months after filing, with no cognitive-improvement claim. Semaglutide has no dementia label, since Novo's 2025 evoke failures stand. The muscle-preserving-combo driver came through an existing product in a new form. No fixed-dose combination has been filed. Lilly sells IV bimagrumab with tirzepatide as a co-marketed clinic bundle under the 2034 adjunct label. Subcutaneous bimagrumab is in phase 2 and not on the market. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 read out in Nov 2036 at a modest benefit, with filing planned for 2037, so there is still no compulsion indication. There is no ageing indication. No new triple agonist was approved. Implants remain in phase 1–2. Net prices still drift down 3–5% a year.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens. Planned drug holidays add re-titration GI episodes: restarters who resume at maintenance dose rather than re-titrating account for a growing share of ED visits for vomiting and dehydration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; no new action.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases are up with volume, and the per-user risk is unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. The first EPI bellwether trial (2035) ended in a defence verdict on causation for a patient with gallstone history, and the next bellwether is set for 2037.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now a recognised population problem. A Sep 2035 JAMA analysis of Medicare claims estimated ~21,000 excess hip fractures in 2034 among beneficiaries 65+ on incretins for more than 2 years (HR ~1.3, ~1.45 after three or more cycles). It also reported that age-adjusted hip-fracture hospitalisation in 65+ had risen ~4% since 2031, reversing a two-decade decline, although the authors could not attribute the whole rise. Sarcopenia diagnosis codes in Medicare users are up ~60% since 2032. Normal-weight longevity users lose lean mass in similar proportion to weight lost, which matters more because they start with less muscle.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained. FDA says current labelling is adequate and has taken no new action. DXA code in use. Bimagrumab is approved as an adjunct but excluded from Part D.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Cohort DXA data (2035–36) show that weight regained after a stop or holiday is ~75–85% fat, while lost weight was ~25–40% lean. Each full cycle therefore leaves users at the same weight with less muscle. This is most pronounced in 65+ and in gray users with supply interruptions. It is now the main mechanistic explanation for the cycle-count fracture gradient.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; professional society guidance (Endocrine Society, AGS) advises against untitrated holidays in 65+.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% of users at weight-loss doses and ~10–11% on retatrutide vs ~3% of controls. The first-year readout of the NIH normal-weight cohort (2036) found clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~4.5% on low-dose plans vs ~3% in controls, a small difference, while ~30% self-reported 'flatness' at least monthly. Symptoms ease within 2–4 weeks of a holiday in most who report them.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. The 2034 consent orders on marketing stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, fastest after retatrutide 12 mg and gray supply interruptions. Short holidays of 2–6 weeks produce partial regain, mostly water and fat.
B12, iron and vitamin D. Low protein intake in older users is now flagged alongside the fracture data.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~2× incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide, with partial recovery after 12+ months off. Tirzepatide excess remains non-significant at 6 years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling; tirzepatide under continued review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; children on drug for decades; repeated cycling; people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~22M current users have a BMI under 30. Cycling effects on bone are now partly characterised (see sarcopenic regain), while effects on the pancreas are not. No final adult height data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; NIH normal-weight cohort reporting.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~70,000 by mid-2036. No repeat of the 2033 insulin-pen cluster at that scale, but ~260 ED visits for hypoglycaemia linked to substituted product in 2035. Gray 'bima' vials tested by two state labs held 0–60% of claimed antibody content, with aggregates and infusion-type reactions after subcutaneous use. Offshore compounded tirzepatide ranged 40–190% of label. Poison-centre calls are ~9× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Existing import alerts retained, with no new alerts, rules or state laws in the window. India's parcel registration took effect Jan 2035 under the 2034 agreement and has been routed around. Federal personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters persists at 48 months. Partial catch-up appears in ~a third of those who stopped. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label monitoring retained; the eleven state bans are unchanged; no new state acted.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab adjunct effects (muscle spasms, acne, diarrhoea; lean-mass gain without proven functional or fracture benefit)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Muscle spasms ~20% and acne ~10% in bundle users. Lean mass is preserved on DXA, but no trial shows fewer falls or fractures, and the 'skinny-frail solved' marketing runs ahead of the data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled under the 2034 adjunct approval; no outcome trial required.

food_and_beverage.state: ~55% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16–18% from 2025, sugary drinks ~14%. Dollar sales are roughly flat on protein and premium lines. The fracture coverage pushed 'bone and muscle' protein and calcium SKUs aimed at 65+ users into Walgreens and Kroger end caps. Value multipacks still carry low-density zips, and in Memphis and the Delta, regain after gray interruptions keeps late-night snack velocity up.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~20% from 2025, beer ~13%. Bar closures continue in mid-sized Midwestern cities. Drug holidays created a small 'off-week' bump that distributors now forecast seasonally around February and the holidays.

restaurants.state: Traffic is slightly down and portion tiers standard. 'Holiday menus' appear in Charlotte and Austin for diners on a planned break. QSR value menus carry low-income markets.

apparel.state: Plus-size mass retail keeps shrinking, but a small independent plus-size revival tied to the body-politics backlash has appeared in Philadelphia, Atlanta and Oakland. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. Hip protectors and 'fall-safe' underwear are a growth line in senior catalogues.

fitness.state: Strength training is the fastest-growing segment. Medicare Advantage plans added resistance-training benefits to fitness programmes after the fracture coverage. Senior centre 'Strong Bones' classes have waiting lists. Premium clinics sell the Lilly 'Strong' infusion bundle plus coaching at $900–1,200 a month all-in.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is down to 23% and monitored tracks to 9%. Coverage concentrates on diabetes and cardiac codes, and employees who lost coverage moved to cash or the mail. Part D premiums rose for 2036, and 2037 bids are up again on dementia-code volume. MA plans tightened prior authorisation for the broadened dementia label, requiring documented BMI and comorbidity.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on tirzepatide's dementia label and the Strong bundle. Novo holds orals and AUD and has no dementia label. Amgen's MariTide lost employer volume and partly recovered in cash. Gray competition is now in next-gen molecules too, and brand counterfeit-defence and litigation spend exceeds $1.3B a year.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Lean and muscled with DXA printouts means covered or rich enough for the Strong bundle. Thin and stooped in an older body now reads as 'skinny-frail', which has become a widely used phrase and a mild slur. Regained-but-softer marks the cycler. In the Delta and in Memphis, the mid-cycle gray body is common. Not taking it at all has become a visible stance in some circles.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Austin and Charlotte the status marker is now lean mass for age, not weight. A high-income 70-year-old shows a grip-strength score the way a 40-year-old shows an HbA1c. Medicare users get the brain drug but pay cash for the muscle drug, so the frail-thin body sorts by income among older adults. Mid-income workers who lost employer coverage went to $219–259 TrumpRx injectables, cheaper orals or the mail.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are shorter and protein-led in high-density zips. Holidays, of both kinds, are when people eat again: 'holiday plates' at Thanksgiving for users on planned breaks. The Bread Alone fasting network has grown to ~1,400 congregations and now frames abstaining from the drug as a fast too. Philadelphia's 'Full Measure' potlucks run as weekly public meals, explicitly drug-free.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Lean-mass verified' is still a premium tier, and a 'no-shot' badge appeared in 2035 and is popular among 30–49 women in Philadelphia and Portland. Couples schedule holidays together around anniversaries and trips.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: The backlash reclaimed appetite as feeling. Full Measure (fat acceptance, founded in Philadelphia in 2035), Unmuted (anti-flatness) and Bread Alone (religious) staged joint 'Feel February' events in 2036 while disagreeing on nearly everything else. Full Measure rejects weight as a health metric; Bread Alone preaches discipline without pharmacy. MAHA legislators praised them, but every restriction bill died in committee. In the upper tier appetite is still noise, while for low-income cyclers it is the sign the package didn't come.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at weight doses and ~10–11% on retatrutide. The NIH normal-weight cohort found ~4.5% on low dose vs 3% in controls, but ~30% of users self-report monthly 'flatness'. ~38% of current users took a planned holiday in 2035–36 and ~25% report a deliberate dose step-down. 'Feel February' drew an estimated ~5M participants in 2036.
interior_life.framing: Mainstream complaint: 'the flats', handled like caffeine dependence or SSRI blunting. Clinicians call it dose-related and manageable, and platforms now sell holiday-friendly schedules. Employers stopped using the word 'steadiness' after the Ohio ruling. Unmuted calls it what the drug does.
interior_life.effect_on_work: The Ohio suit survived the motion to dismiss in Jul 2035 and is in discovery. HR departments retreated from steadiness language, and calm-fee reimbursement fell to 13% of large employers. Promotion-rate data are no longer circulated internally. Workers now ask for 'holiday weeks' informally, and some managers expect slower output during them. Columbus-corridor 3PLs quietly dropped track-linked shift-lead criteria.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday' became a genre: songs, stand-up sets and short films about the first week off. Sportsbook handle per account recovers ~5–8% in February and the December holidays, and operators now time promotions to them. Off nights have spread to Pittsburgh and Atlanta.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Planned holidays have become a sexual calendar: couples' therapists report 'holiday sex' and the arguments that follow when desire returns unevenly. Desire mismatch is still the leading complaint, now discussed openly.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The dementia label made incretins a seniors' issue. AARP lobbies CMS to cover bimagrumab, and Part D premium growth became campaign material in 2036 House races. Restriction bills in 2035–36 sessions in Georgia, Kentucky and Arizona all died, opposed by pharmacy, telehealth and employer lobbies and split by the backlash itself. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Static. No new state laws, federal rules or consent orders in 2035–36. The eleven 2034 under-12 bans and the seven states' in-person rules stand unchanged. The FDA approved the tirzepatide dementia broadening and judged existing bone and muscle labelling adequate. Enforcement against gray supply continued at 2034 levels.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx prices are manufacturer-set. The Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 30% wellness guidance stands. CMS's exclusion of bimagrumab as a weight-loss adjunct is long-standing policy applied, not a new rule.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. Data flows continue under consent, but cohort analytics sales slowed as employers backed away amid discovery in the Ohio case. Two Medicaid programmes still condition coverage.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT's 2033 guidance is unchanged. The Army oral pilot continues. TRICARE is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's B2C export registration took effect Jan 2035. Direct Indian parcels fell ~30%, and volume rerouted through Dubai and Kathmandu consolidators. Chinese biologics fronts added activin-antibody 'bima' to the reta trade. There is no CBP mail agreement. The cash-to-generic gap is still ~40–60×.

events.event: Lilly's tirzepatide dementia trial reports 19% lower all-cause dementia risk over three and a half years; Lilly files in May to drop the heart-disease requirement from the label
Lilly launches 'Strong', a $599-a-month cash bundle of Zepbound and monthly bimagrumab infusions sold through clinics as the end of 'skinny-frail'; Medicare says it will not pay for the infusion
Federal judge in Ohio refuses to dismiss call-centre agent's suit over promotions favouring monitored-track enrollees; by November only 25% of employers still cover weight-loss drugs, down from 29%
JAMA study of Medicare claims attributes about 21,000 hip fractures a year to long-term incretin use and finds regain after each stop is mostly fat; FDA says current warnings are adequate

Gray-market incretin users pass 20 million as offshore-licensed telehealth prescribers and Dubai-routed parcels replace direct Indian shipments, and 'reta-bima' stack kits appear on longevity storefronts

FDA broadens tirzepatide's dementia-risk label to adults 60 and over with obesity or overweight plus a cardiometabolic condition; Part D plans brace for millions of new claims, months after an estimated five million users joined 'Feel February' drug holidays led by Full Measure, Unmuted and Bread Alone

open_tensions: Medicare now pays for the brain drug but not the muscle drug. Older users on tirzepatide's dementia label carry the established fracture gradient, and bimagrumab sits behind a weight-loss exclusion and a $599 cash bundle, with no outcome trial showing it prevents a single fall.
Drug holidays are now normal, and the cycling data say each full cycle trades muscle for fat at the same weight. The practice that relieves the flats may be driving the fracture curve.
Employers retreated from coverage, and some of their former enrollees went to the mail. Gray use is 24.5M and now includes next-gen and antibody products, while no government acted in the window.
The Ohio suit is in discovery on whether favouring adherence-verified 'steady' workers is disability discrimination, while the 30% adherence premium guidance it sits beside still stands.

prose.headline: The Brain Shot Got Covered. The Muscle Shot Didn't. America at 36 Percent, One Hip at a Time.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about ninety-nine million American adults take an incretin drug, more than a third of the country. Nearly half have tried one. The growth did not come from employers, who retreated. Only 23 percent of them still pay for weight-loss use, down from 29 two years ago. Monitored metabolic tracks shrank after a federal judge in Ohio let a call-centre agent's discrimination suit go forward, and the companies that had promoted 'steady' workers stopped circulating the numbers. People who lost coverage did not stop. They moved to the cash channel, where TrumpRx injectables now cost $219 to $259 a month and starting pills are still $149, or to the mail.

The mail is bigger than ever. India's new export registration took effect in 2035, and the parcels now come through Dubai and Kathmandu instead. Offshore-licensed telehealth doctors write 'personalised' compounded tirzepatide and retatrutide prescriptions that no American board reviews. Longevity storefronts sell kits pairing Chinese 'reta' vials with 'bima', a knock-off of the new muscle antibody, whose content runs from nothing to roughly half the label. About one user in four is on product no regulator has seen. No legislature or agency did anything new about it.

The biggest new public spending is on the brain. In March 2035 Lilly's dementia trial showed tirzepatide cutting all-cause dementia risk by about a fifth, and in June 2036 the FDA dropped the requirement that patients already have heart disease. Medicare cannot pay for weight loss, but it can pay for dementia risk, and Part D now covers some eighteen million users at an annual run rate above $46 billion. Six million of them qualify on the dementia code. Retired schoolteachers and bus drivers take the same weekly pen as Charlotte executives, for their memory.

The brain label arrived as the muscle bill came due. A JAMA analysis in September 2035 put the excess at about twenty-one thousand hip fractures a year among long-term older users. It also explained why cycling made fractures worse: weight lost includes a good deal of muscle, and weight regained is almost all fat. 'Skinny-frail' became a household phrase. Lilly's answer, already on the market, was Strong: Zepbound plus a monthly infusion of bimagrumab, $599 a month in cash plus the clinic fee, sold as the end of frailty. The bundle preserves lean mass on a scan, and no trial yet shows it prevents falls. Medicare classes the infusion as a weight-loss adjunct and will not pay. An older user's chance of being thin and strong rather than thin and stooped now depends on whether they can pay for the muscle drug, since Medicare already pays for the brain drug.

The complaint about flatness went mainstream. A large federal cohort found real anhedonia only slightly raised on low doses, but nearly a third of users say they feel flat at least monthly, and people now treat it like coffee dependence, with a step-down or a holiday. 'Feel February' drew an estimated five million people off their drugs for a month. Its organisers were a strange coalition: Philadelphia's Full Measure, a fat-acceptance revival with weekly public potlucks; Unmuted, which calls the drug a sedative; and Bread Alone, the church fasting network, now fourteen hundred congregations. They agree on almost nothing except February. Restriction bills in three states died in committee.

The economy has adjusted rather than broken. Snack volumes are down a sixth, spirits a fifth. Medicare Advantage plans added strength classes, and senior centres in Dayton keep waiting lists for them. Sportsbooks schedule promotions for the weeks when bettors are off their drugs. Couples plan holidays around anniversaries. Most people look healthier than they did ten years ago, and more older people are falling.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Carol Wenzel, sixty-eight, sets the pen against her belly at 7:10 on a Tuesday, the way the nurse showed her in July. Seven point five. Forty-seven dollars copay; the pharmacist called it 'the memory one' and she let him.

Her mother didn't know her for the last four years. Carol doesn't think about that while she pushes the button. She thinks about the bruise from last week, which is the wrong colour.

Breakfast is Greek yogurt with a scoop of the calcium protein from the Kroger end cap. Half the cup. She writes '22 g' on the fridge sheet because the Strong Bones instructor at the Dayton senior centre asks.

At class she does sit-to-stands holding a chair. Twelve. Then ten. The woman beside her, Lorraine, has the clinic bundle, the infusion on Thursdays, and arms like a girl's. Lorraine's son pays. Carol asked her doctor about the infusion and he said Medicare calls it weight-loss, then said 'I'm sorry' in a way that meant five-ninety-nine.

Her daughter Jess calls at lunch from the warehouse in Groveport. The company dropped coverage in January. Jess is on vials now, from a man on Telegram, and she has been on a holiday since the package didn't come. 'I feel great,' Jess says, and she sounds it, which worries Carol more.

In the afternoon Carol does the crossword in pen. She finishes it.

At dusk she takes the trash down the porch steps one at a time, hand on the rail, the way the DXA man said. The bag is light. She is careful anyway.
